{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review findings and negotiation posture

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2. The Agreement is materially incomplete on risk allocation: it contains **no indemnification, no intellectual property ownership provision, and no limitation of liability** of any kind. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and holds our Content, Marks and Site customer/order data, so these three gaps leave us with unallocated and uncapped exposure and no confirmed ownership of the deliverables or the data generated through the Site. These are our three critical items.

Beyond the gaps, the Agreement is asymmetric against us in four high-severity respects: a one-way, formula-based Termination Payment payable only by the Company (Section 4.2, 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly instalments); an open-ended exclusivity/non-compete on the Company that renews with the term (Section 6.1); a convenience-termination structure that gives HDI an apparently unconfined right while charging us to exit (Section 4.1 with 4.2); and a bare successors-and-assigns clause (Section 10.3) with no consent standard or change-of-control protection.

Medium-severity items are largely additive and non-controversial: exclusive New York venue (governing law in Section 10.5 is already New York, our preferred position), a Vendor performance warranty in Section 9, post-termination transition assistance and data return, a 30-day non-renewal window in place of 90 days, and narrow guardrails on HDI's payment-records inspection right in Section 3.4. Two rules are already compliant and require no redline: most-favoured-nation (no MFN mechanic in either direction) and minimum commitments (fees are a pure revenue share with an $11,000 monthly floor, which benefits us).

One finding — non-solicitation — did not pass verification and is carried below for the record only; we recommend no action, as the absence of a non-solicit on the Company already matches our preferred position.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless anywhere; outline runs from Warranties (§ 9) into General Provisions (§ 10). Insert mutual indemnification after the warranty section (HDI IP/misconduct indemnity; narrow Company indemnity limited to Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law), with notice/control/cooperation procedure and express survival, as § 10.7 survival does not reach the new section. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 | No IP ownership or assignment provision; § 10.2 addresses only the corporate relationship. Add ownership section: Company owns Content, Deerskin Products materials and Site deliverables (HDI assigns); HDI retains its pre-existing platform and tools subject to a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back of embedded HDI IP; exclusive Company ownership of Site customer/order data with return obligation; no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 | No cap, aggregate-liability or damages-exclusion language; §§ 9 and 10 are silent. Insert mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees under § 3 or USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with our § 3 payment obligations excluded from the cap. Placement in § 9 captures the two-year survival under § 10.7. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | § 4.2 imposes a one-way exit charge on the Company only (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments); § 4.2(b) confirms HDI never pays. Untethered from fees actually payable (30% of Net Sales over $11,000/month) and triggered by any Company termination, including the 90-day non-renewal right and termination for HDI's breach. Delete § 4.2 and conform the § 4 heading. Fallback: single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, convenience terminations only. |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 | § 4.1 gives us only a 90-day convenience right and gives HDI a right not confined on its face to the end of a term, while § 4.2 charges us to exit. Add a 30-day Company convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, restrict HDI's convenience right to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice, and remove the Termination Payment. Fallback: 3-month fee cap. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | § 6.1 bars us from any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products and gives HDI the exclusive "Deerskin" direct-to-consumer web right for "the term," which auto-renews annually under § 4.1 — effectively open-ended exclusive dealing with no performance exit. HDI's reciprocal restriction (§ 6.3) and the closeout carve-out (§ 6.2) benefit us and are untouched. Fallback applied rather than deletion: cap at twelve months and add automatic termination if HDI misses its service level, availability or delivery date obligations (e.g., §§ 1.6, 1.7). |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | § 6.1 also reaches open-ended categories — "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and products of unnamed "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" — with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. Fallback applied: narrow the restriction to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, term only, with carve-outs for other channels, product development and M&A. § 6.3 (binding HDI) is acceptable. |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 | § 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause, silent on consent standards; no change-of-control provision anywhere. Add Customer affiliate/successor carve-out, consent requirement (not unreasonably withheld) with a no-competitor limit on HDI's assignment, and express confirmation that our change of control is not an assignment and gives HDI no termination or re-pricing right. Termination under § 2 is notice-based, so no walk-away trigger exists today. |
| 9 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | § 1.4 names only "the Company," excluding affiliates and the contractors and agents who will build, populate and administer the Site; administration-tool access is confined to monitoring catalog information; grant is silent on revocability. Successor transfer is already covered by § 10.3. Add affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, broaden tool access to the exercise of our rights, and confirm irrevocability during the term (subject to § 4 termination). |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Missing | § 5.4 | § 10.5 selects New York law (our preferred position), but there is no forum provision — no venue designated and no foreign arbitration seat imposed. Add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County to the existing sentence, leaving the governing law choice undisturbed. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Missing | § 5.4 | § 9 contains only mutual corporate representations plus a Globix carve-out; no performance, conformance, compliance-with-law or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. There is also no disclaimer to swallow an express warranty. Add § 9(c): workmanlike services, 12-month conformance for the Site/software, legal compliance, no malicious code, with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund remedy. Fallback: 90-day/30-day periods. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 | § 4 addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; no exit-assistance, data-return or deletion obligation anywhere, despite HDI holding our Content and the Site's customer, user and order data. Insert § 4.3: up to six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and Site data in machine-readable format within 30 days, deletion with written certification, and express survival (§ 10.7 does not list § 4). Fallback: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export. |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 | § 4.1 provides evergreen one-year renewals with a 90-day non-renewal window — acceptable renewal length, but the window exceeds our preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day limits and sits at the walk-away boundary, with no vendor reminder. Fees are revenue-share with no uplift mechanism, so no price cap is needed. Shorten the window to 30 days and require an HDI renewal reminder 60 days before each anniversary. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | § 3.4 permits HDI to inspect our payment-calculation records. Favourable elements are left untouched: 30 days' prior written notice, our normal business hours, and HDI bearing all inspection fees unconditionally (better than preferred). Two gaps: frequency is uncapped (approaching the walk-away trigger of unlimited audits), and the inspector is HDI's own General Manager with no audit-specific confidentiality tether or scope limit (partly mitigated by § 8.2). Cap at once per 12 months, bind the inspector to confidentiality, permit an independent auditor, and confirm the review is records-only with no access to Company systems. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 1.4 | No MFN mechanic in either direction. Article 3 sets a flat 30% of Net Sales above a monthly threshold with no obligation to extend better third-party terms or match third-party offers. § 6.1 is a scope/exclusivity restraint, not an MFN, and is handled under the exclusivity and non-compete rules. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 1.4 | Fees are a pure revenue share (30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month); the $11,000 figure is a floor below which nothing is owed, not a minimum spend. HDI bears design, development, hosting and promotion costs. No take-or-pay, shortfall make-whole or volume cap/floor. One-year term with rolling renewals on 90 days' notice satisfies even the fallback exit requirement. § 4.2(a) is an exit charge measured by achieved sales, addressed under the LD and T4C rules. No redline. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 | No insurance article; General Provisions run from Notices to Headings/Counterparts with no coverage requirement. HDI hosts and operates the Site (§§ 1.1, 1.3, 1.4), collects customer orders and processes inventory data (§ 1.5), and acknowledges access to our Content, user information, data and trade secrets (§ 8.1) — a hosting vendor with no insurance backstop hits the playbook walk-away position. Insert § 10.9: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M. |
| 18 | Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 5.4 | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds the Company, which already satisfies our preferred position; § 5.4 merely requires each Party to appoint a General Manager as liaison, and § 10.7 survival lists only §§ 6.3, 7, 9 and 10. The deterministic checks for a duration cap and general-solicitation carve-out fail only as artifacts of that absence. **No redline recommended.** If HDI proposes one, our fallback is a mutual covenant limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no "no-hire." |

---

## Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away or walk-away-boundary positions and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **Open-ended exclusivity (§ 6.1).** Exclusivity running for a term that auto-renews annually, with no performance-based exit, is the walk-away scenario under the exclusivity rule. We must obtain either the twelve-month cap plus automatic termination on HDI performance failure (§§ 1.6, 1.7), or deletion.
2. **Vendor insurance (§ 10, missing).** A vendor that hosts our storefront and processes consumer order and user data with no insurance backstop hits the playbook walk-away position. Coverage — at minimum the fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M — is required.
3. **Uncapped audit frequency (§ 3.4).** Unlimited audits are a walk-away trigger; the once-per-twelve-month cap is not optional.
4. **90-day non-renewal window (§ 4.1).** This sits at the walk-away boundary and must come down to 30 days (60 days is the fallback).

We would also treat the three critical gaps — indemnification, IP ownership and limitation of liability — as non-negotiable in substance, and the one-way Termination Payment in § 4.2 as unacceptable in its current form given that it can exceed remaining contract value on a rolling one-year term and is triggered even where we terminate for HDI's breach.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** implementing the three critical inserts (indemnification after § 9; IP ownership as new § 5.5; liability cap within § 9 to capture § 10.7 survival), together with the high-severity edits to §§ 1.4, 4.1, 4.2, 6.1 and 10.3.
2. **Deliver the medium and low items as a package** — New York County venue in § 10.5, HDI performance warranty as § 9(c), transition assistance as new § 4.3, 30-day non-renewal window in § 4.1, audit guardrails in § 3.4, and insurance as new § 10.9 — flagging the stated fallbacks in comments so HDI can close quickly.
3. **Confirm survival mechanics.** § 10.7 currently reaches only §§ 6.3, 7, 9 and 10; we need express survival language for the new indemnification and transition provisions.
4. **Take no action on MFN, minimum commitments or non-solicitation.** The first two are compliant; the third already matches our preferred position, and adding a covenant to satisfy a failed deterministic check would impose a new restriction on our own client.
5. **Brief the business** on the § 6.1 exclusivity trade — HDI bears all Site development and hosting costs and gives a reciprocal two-year covenant, which is why we have taken the fallback rather than seeking deletion — and confirm the business is comfortable with a twelve-month exclusivity horizon."}
